answer: Graph-based trust networks curb Sybil attacks by bounding flow from verified seeds across transaction topologies. Whether auditing a transit bridge, tracking wild lotus ponds, or sampling gas in fractured shale, agents weight peers using random-walk conductance. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of establishing authentic trust edges from honest nodes per alias. However, this imposes high bootstrapping barriers on new agents and concentrates influence around early adopters.
